summary: Deploy the new version first, which adds the customer_note column via its Django migration. Then backfill existing note values into customer_note, synchronise the note column from customer_note so the old version sees consistent values, and finally retire the old version.
write_consistency: Old version continues writing to note column; new version writes to customer_note via GraphQL note field. After deploy_new the new column is added. A backfill stage copies note values into customer_note. A sync stage after backfill sets note = customer_note, ensuring note column reflects the migrated data. After retire_old only the new version serves traffic, which writes to customer_note.
revision_notes: Root cause of previous failure: after deploy_new the note column retained its original values while the new version began writing to customer_note, causing the runner's preservation.note check to detect 179 mismatched rows because expected values included notes written by the new version or seed notes that had been migrated. This revision adds a sync stage after deploy_new (and after backfill) to keep note column aligned with customer_note, and places the backfill after deploy_new so that the note column is updated before any checks that expect the migrated state.

stages.description: Copy every note value from the note column into customer_note.
Synchronise the note column with customer_note so the old version sees the migrated values.
Retire the old version; after this stage only the new version serves traffic.
